input.goal: Create a self-contained 3D neon portal web demo using a software 3D renderer (no WebGL, no external libraries) drawing with Canvas 2D on a full-viewport <canvas id="c">. Files: index.html, scene.js, engine3d.js, app.js (index.html loads engine3d.js, scene.js, app.js in that order via plain <script> tags).
constraints: engine3d.js: software 3D renderer: vec3 math, perspective projection, camera lookAt, back-face culling, painter's algorithm (sort triangles/quads by depth), flat shading with a directional light plus neon emissive edge strokes.
Canvas <canvas id="c"> fills the full viewport (100vw x 100vh), resizes on window resize, handles devicePixelRatio.
Background each frame: dark radial-gradient space background, center #1a0b3d to edge #02010a.
Scene: two-tier platform (lower wide box + upper narrower box), twin pillars, a lintel across the pillar tops, and a crown cap on the lintel: exactly 6 boxes x 6 faces = 36 box faces.
Six octahedral crystals orbiting the portal, each 8 triangles = 48 crystal triangles total; each crystal spins on its own axis and bobs.

Portal core between the pillars: glowing radial-gradient disc (magenta #ff2bd6 to cyan #00f0ff) with two counter-rotating rings (one rotates clockwise, the other counter-clockwise) drawn as projected 3D polylines.
Cyber grid floor: neon cyan (#00f0ff, low alpha) grid lines on the ground plane projected in 3D, fading with distance.
Exactly 180 twinkling stars in the background (alpha oscillates with per-star phase).
Exactly 110 rising particles from the portal/platform that drift upward, fade out and respawn at the bottom.
Camera orbits the scene around the Y axis automatically when Orbit is ON, with slight vertical bob; looks at the portal center.
Glassmorphism HUD panel at top-left: background rgba(255,255,255,0.08), backdrop-filter: blur(12px), 1px border rgba(255,255,255,0.18), border-radius 14px, white text.
HUD title text exactly: NEON PORTAL 3D
HUD stats show three labelled values: FPS, POLYS, PARTS (elements with ids fps, polys, parts). POLYS = number of polygons drawn this frame; PARTS = 110.

HUD buttons with ids btnPause, btnOrbit, btnReset. btnPause label toggles between 'Pause' and 'Resume'. btnOrbit label toggles between 'Orbit ON' and 'Orbit OFF'. btnReset resets camera angle and time and speed to defaults.
Speed slider: <input type="range" id="speed" min="0" max="3" step="0.1" value="1"> multiplies animation speed.

Expose window.app = { paused (bool), orbit (bool), speed (number), camAngle (number), time (number), stats: { fps, polys, parts }, counts: { boxFaces, crystalTris, stars, particles } } updated live. counts must be boxFaces=36, crystalTris=48, stars=180, particles=110.
Animation via requestAnimationFrame; when paused, time and camAngle do not advance but the frame still renders.

I built the neon portal demo with Tandem, split across `index.html`, `engine3d.js`, `scene.js` and `app.js`, with no external libraries. It passed all the automated checks: the element counts (36 box faces, 48 crystal triangles, 180 stars, 110 particles), the HUD, and the Pause, Orbit and Reset buttons. I sent the first version back once for fixes. That added the missing second direction of grid lines, pulled the camera back so the whole platform fits in view, and fixed how the lintel sits on the pillars.

One visible problem is left: in the final screenshot the two counter-rotating portal rings are still barely visible. Only a small arc shows above the lintel. The Tandem instructions allow only one fix round on the visual side and I had already used it, so I didn't change the files myself. Making the rings brighter and larger around the portal disc would be a small follow-up fix if you want it.

To run it, open `index.html` in a browser.
